standard_prerequisites.name: Poisson--Dirichlet process
standard_prerequisites.statement: The normalised points V_i = X_i/S of a Poisson process on the positive half-line with intensity e^{-x}/x dx form a Poisson--Dirichlet process.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the representation adopted at source line 1131.

standard_prerequisites.name: Colouring theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: Randomly colouring the points of a Poisson process with k colours yields independent Poisson processes with intensities p_i times the original intensity.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source line 1131 to split the process into the k coloured subprocesses Pi_m.

standard_prerequisites.name: Campbell's theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a Poisson process, the Laplace transform of the sum of a functional over the points is the exponential of the corresponding integral.
standard_prerequisites.use: It computes the moment generating function of S_m at source lines 1139-1142.

core_obligations: Represent the Poisson--Dirichlet process through the points X_i of a Poisson process with intensity e^{-x}/x dx on the positive half-line, setting V_i := X_i/S where S is the total sum (source line 1131).
Apply the colouring theorem to obtain independent Poisson processes Pi_m of intensity alpha_m e^{-x}/x dx for m = 1,...,k (source lines 1132-1138).

Compute the moment generating function of S_m with Campbell's theorem and evaluate the integral to obtain -alpha_m log(1-s), which is the moment generating function of a Gamma(alpha_m,1) variable (source lines 1139-1143).

Identify the vector of sums over colour classes, normalised by the total, with the Dirichlet distribution Dir(alpha), using the standard characterisation of the Dirichlet law as normalised independent Gamma variables (source lines 1143-1147).

proof_roadmap.step: Poisson representation of the Poisson--Dirichlet process and colouring of its points.
Independence and intensities of the coloured subprocesses.
Moment generating function of each coloured sum by Campbell's theorem.
Normalise to obtain the Dirichlet law.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:probabilistic dirichlet law` at source lines 1121-1128: colouring the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet process independently with probabilities alpha_j yields a random vector distributed according to Dir(alpha). The author's proof (source lines 1130-1148), repeated from Donnelly and Tavare because the Poisson representation is needed later, is a two-tool computation: the colouring theorem turns the single Poisson process into k independent processes of intensities alpha_m e^{-x}/x dx (lines 1131-1138), and Campbell's theorem evaluates the Laplace transform of each coloured sum, producing the integral of (e^{sx}-1)e^{-x}/x whose value -alpha_m log(1-s) identifies a Gamma(alpha_m,1) law (lines 1139-1143). The Dirichlet conclusion then follows by normalising the independent Gamma sums (lines 1144-1147). Both cited theorems are structural, and neither the colouring representation nor the generating-function computation is visible from the statement.
